children: U.S. equity averages extended their advance Friday afternoon as crude prices retreated on reports that Washington and Tehran had shifted their discussions from opening contacts to a more technical stage.
fell about 3% to roughly $91.70 a barrel, while Brent
slipped about 4% to near $103.33, as traders priced in a possible path toward restoring commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

Al Jazeera’s Tehran bureau chief, Nourddine Dgheir, said sources in the Iranian capital described the tone as increasingly constructive. The Qatari-owned network reported that technical specialists had joined the New York talks after an initial session involving U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Qatar has mediated between the two governments for months.

Moreover, U.S. officials did not immediately confirm that the negotiations had moved to the technical level. Even so, the combination of lower energy prices and the prospect of a sequenced reopening of the waterway supported another bid higher in the major stock indexes as investors weighed whether diplomacy could ease a key supply risk.

title: Stocks climb as Hormuz talks turn technical and oil slides
